sections.html:
Conway County lies in the Arkansas River Valley of central Arkansas, about 52 miles northwest of Little Rock. Morrilton is the county seat and largest city, with 6,992 residents in 2020. Plumerville and Oppelo are the incorporated towns. Conway the city is a different place, in Faulkner County to the east.

Census takers found 20,715 people in 8,387 households in 2020, and the 2025 estimate stands at 21,393. Vacancy hit 13.1 percent of the 9,646 housing units, and owners live in 73.2 percent of the occupied ones. Population slid 2.6 percent over the decade ending in 2020. Median age is 42.1, and 30.6 percent of residents live in urban areas. Most county offices, the courts and the assessor are in Morrilton, where Interstate 40 runs along the north side of the city and US 64 is the main road through downtown.

Manufacturing matters to demand. Green Bay Packaging announced a project of more than $1 billion at its Morrilton mill in June 2025, with 35 new jobs and a mill that already employs more than 620 people in the county.

The assessor and the collector share one address, 117 S. Moose Street in Morrilton, AR 72110. Assessor hours run Monday through Friday, 8:00 to 4:30, and the number is (501) 354-9622. Under section 26-26-715 the assessor must keep appraisal and assessment records current, so a change in land use or a new improvement should lead to an updated value.

The county collector collects property taxes for the county, its municipalities, the public schools, the library and improvement districts. Both offices link to the actDataScout vendor for tax and real estate record searches. The state is moving counties to a four-year reappraisal cycle, so ask the assessor when this county's next one falls. Yearly increases stop at 5 percent on a primary residence and 10 percent on commercial property.

Your application to the county equalization board is due by the third Monday in August. Hearings under section 26-27-317 must start by the second Monday of that month, and you can attend in person or submit documents instead.

  • Expect a written decision at least ten business days after the hearing.
  • That notice has to explain your right to go to county court and give the deadline.
  • Evidence that reaches the assessor fewer than five business days before the hearing may cause a continuance.
  • A petition filed for a business entity must be signed and filed by an Arkansas attorney.

Collectors across Arkansas generally set October 15 as the deadline and add a 10 percent penalty afterward. Phone Conway County's collector for this county's dates and payment methods, and ask if any older years are still open on the parcel.

Land with unpaid tax may in time be certified to the Commissioner of State Lands, who has to notify the owner and offer redemption. Under section 26-37-301 the owner, or a person with no ownership interest, redeems by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs, notice costs included.

  • No sale can occur until a year after certification.
  • Notice goes by certified mail first, then by regular mail if the certified letter is unclaimed or refused.
  • If a homestead owner cannot be shown to have received it, personal service is required at least 60 days before the sale.

Calling the collector sooner gets you a payoff number while choices remain.

Back tax gets settled inside the sale. The collector tells you what is owed, penalty included, and the title company pays that from your proceeds when you close. Bring the deed and photo ID. If the owner has died and no probate has started, expect the title company to ask who has authority to sign before it can close.

First, decide whether to list with an agent or ask a cash buyer for an offer. Second, get the numbers: the tax balance from the collector and the assessed values from the assessor. Third, gather the deed and any records of repairs. Fourth, once an offer is accepted, the title company searches the record for liens and unpaid tax and sets the signing date. Fifth, you sign the deed, the county is paid from your proceeds and the sale is recorded.

Vacant houses and inherited houses need extra care. Utilities should stay on so a buyer can inspect the house, the roof and crawl space should be checked for water, and every heir should be reachable. A cash buyer can often work around these problems, but the title company still needs every signature.

sections.h2: Pricing a house that has been empty
sections.html:
A house that has sat vacant carries a discount in buyers' minds, so address it directly. Turn the water and power on for showings, clear debris from the yard, and have someone check for leaks and pests. Photos taken in daylight with the lights on do more than a long description. Be upfront about repairs and their cost, a buyer who finds a problem late tends to ask for a bigger credit than the repair would cost.

Some owners also ask a friend or neighbor to open the house for showings when they live far away. If cash is tight, selling as-is to a cash buyer avoids spending money on work you may not recoup.

Keep the deed, the latest tax statement, any notice from the equalization board and receipts for work done on the house in one folder. If the owner died, add the death certificate and any court papers. If the house is a rental, add the lease and a note on the tenant's status. Updating the assessor on improvements ahead of time avoids surprises, since the assessor must keep records current when improvements change.

With 13.1 percent of housing units vacant, many sellers here are dealing with houses that have sat empty. Morrilton gets about 51.20 inches of precipitation a year, so roofs, gutters and crawl spaces take steady moisture, and buyers look closely at them.

  • Houses sitting vacant after a death or a move.
  • Owners who cannot find the cash for roof, foundation or plumbing repairs.
  • Rental properties with a tenant who has left or stopped paying.
  • Back taxes tied to a probate that has not started.

A cash sale takes the house as it is and clears taxes from the proceeds, so repairs and the lender's appraisal do not hold up the closing.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Conway County property tax?
faqs.a: At the county collector's office at 117 S. Moose Street in Morrilton, AR 72110. An online tax record search is also available through actDataScout.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Conway County assessment?
faqs.a: The third Monday in August under Ark. Code 26-27-317. The application goes to the county equalization board, which must start hearing appeals by the second Monday in August.
About 567 square miles, among the smallest counties in Arkansas. It had 20,715 residents in the 2020 census.

faqs.q: Is Conway County the same as the city of Conway?
faqs.a: No. Conway County's seat is Morrilton. The city of Conway is in Faulkner County, which borders Conway County to the east.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Conway County with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the collector for the amount owed, including penalty, and settle it as part of the sale.
